Subject: Next steps — embeddings integration & migration plan (NimbleCart)

Hi Alex / Lara — thanks again for the call earlier today. Great to hear more about the search & recommendations use cases and the migration constraints you mentioned. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align the team: 

Summary of what we heard
- Current setup: NimbleCart is using VectraAI embeddings (1024 dims) + a vendor-hosted ANN index for product search + a reranker service.
- Primary goals: improve semantic relevance for long product descriptions, reduce per-query tail latency to <120ms, and avoid a full reindex blackout during migration.
- Constraints: PCI-adjacent data, strict data-retention policy, and a mid-quarter procurement window.

Key technical questions we need to confirm
1) Target embedding dimensionality: you asked about 768 vs 1536 tradeoffs for your catalog size (~6M items).
2) Migration approach: full re-embed vs incremental backfill and whether to keep old index live during cutover.
3) Batching/latency: target per-request batching limits and acceptable cold-start latency.
4) Normalization & similarity metric: cosine with L2 normalization or dot-product?
5) Auth & routing: preferred auth (API key vs OIDC) and region, and whether traffic should route to dedicated capacity or hosted.

Proposed next steps (action items)
- Redwood (Hannah): schedule a technical run-through with Marissa (solutions engineer) to map the migration runbook and confirm API/SDK onboarding. Suggested slot: Tue 2027-03-23 10:00am PST.
- NimbleCart (Alex): share a ~1k sample of product vectors + original content (anonymized) and the current index metrics (recall@k / qps distribution).
- Redwood (Marissa): prepare a one-page ops runbook covering incremental backfill, A/B rollout, and rollback criteria; include FAISS config and ANN tuning notes.

Attachments we will share: nimblecart-embeddings-runbook.pdf (migration phases + rollback), redwood-sdk-snippets.md (auth examples + batching patterns), redwood-cost-estimate.csv (ballpark token and hosting costs).

Open questions I flagged for the internal team: Ben — can you pull the Dedicated capacity latency SLO comparison for 1/4/8 GPU pools?

If that sounds right I’ll book the run-through with Marissa and include a short agenda. Thanks — Hannah

Thanks Hannah — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we lock the run-through: 

- Dimensionality: our team is biased toward 1024 because it preserved compatibility with our current ANN settings, but we keep hearing 1536 improves recall for longer texts. Can you summarize the tradeoffs (cost / index size / latency)?
- Migration: we cannot have >15% of traffic dropped during cutover. An incremental shadow re-embed approach sounds promising — do you have run times for backfilling 6M items on a typical dedicated pool?
- Batching: our peak qps is bursty (up to 600 qps). We want to avoid per-request latencies >120ms p50. How do batching strategies interact with that SLO?

We'll prep a 1k sample and an anonymized query distribution and upload by EOD Monday (2027-03-22). Procurement cc'd for timeline visibility.

Subject: Re: Next steps — embeddings integration & migration plan (NimbleCart)

Alex — great questions. I pulled together a concise technical note below and attached a short runbook + SDK snippets. TL;DR answers first, details after.

TL;DR
- Dimensionality: recommend evaluating 1536 for the customer-facing semantic reranker, but keep 1024 for a lightweight cold-start index if cost/latency is tight. We suggest an A/B with 1536 on ~10% of traffic.
- Migration/backfill: incremental backfill on a 4-GPU dedicated pool typically completes ~200–350k re-embeds/hour depending on sequence length and quantization. For 6M items expect ~18–30 hours of steady backfill (parallelizable across regions).
- Batching & latency: per-request batching reduces per-token overhead but increases tail latency if you wait to batch. For your bursty 600 qps, aim for dynamic batching with max batch size 32 and a 10ms micro-batching window — we see good p50/p90 tradeoffs under that config.
- Normalization & metric: use L2 normalization + cosine similarity when combining with BM25 scores (cosine is robust when you normalize). Dot-product is okay if you store un-normalized vectors and use explicit inner-product optimized indices.
- Reranker pattern: hybrid = BM25 retrieve (top 200) -> embedding rerank (top 50) -> lightweight learned reranker. Keeps recall high and rerank cost low.

Details / migration runbook highlights
1) Snapshot and staging: export current index (metadata + vector pointers), stand up a shadow ANN cluster (FAISS HNSW recommended) in a staging VPC.
2) Embedding strategy: generate 1536-d vectors for new embeddings; run a pilot re-embed of a 50k slice to validate recall and index size. If memory/latency impact is too high, we fallback to 1024 with quantization (INT8/FP16).
3) Backfill plan: incremental backfill with write-ahead queue to avoid locking; perform re-embed in windows (off-peak) and migrate alias on the index once quality gate passes. Keep old index live with weighted routing for canary traffic.
4) ANN tuning: HNSW ef_search 128 / ef_construction 200 recommended starting point; adjust ef_search up for higher recall. Use product quantization only if memory is the limiting factor.
5) SDK & auth: Redwood SDK supports API key and OIDC; for NimbleCart's PCI-adjacent data we recommend OIDC with short-lived tokens and private VPC peering (we'll provide OIDC setup doc in redwood-sdk-snippets.md).

Cost/size notes
- 1536-d vectors ~1.5x storage of 1024-d. With Faiss & FP16 expect ~18–25 GB per million vectors raw (varies with quantization).
- Estimate attached in redwood-cost-estimate.csv with example dedicated pool pricing.

Attachments: nimblecart-embeddings-runbook.pdf (detailed phased checklist), redwood-sdk-snippets.md (auth + batching patterns + sample curl/SDK calls), redwood-cost-estimate.csv (ballpark). Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1Xr-Embed-Migration-NimbleCart

Next steps I suggest: the run-through on Tue 2027-03-23 10:00am PST, bring a sample query set and any privacy constraints. I can run the pilot embed on a 50k slice we provide.
